nodes.label: Agent memory
nodes.rationale: Persistent, queryable state read and written across sessions so the agent does not start from zero each time.

nodes.label: Cypher
nodes.rationale: Declarative query language for FalkorDB; patterns drawn as ASCII art to match or create graph structure.

nodes.label: Edge (relationship)
nodes.rationale: A typed, directed connection between two nodes that itself carries meaning and can hold properties.

nodes.label: Graph database
nodes.rationale: Stores data as nodes and relationships and traverses them directly rather than joining tables.

nodes.label: GraphRAG
nodes.rationale: RAG in which retrieved context is a subgraph traversed by relationships, not loose text chunks.

nodes.label: MERGE
nodes.rationale: The Cypher clause that matches a pattern or creates it if absent, the basis of idempotent memory writes.

nodes.label: Node
nodes.rationale: A single entity in the graph, optionally carrying properties.

nodes.label: Three-tier memory model
nodes.rationale: Composition of episodic, semantic, and procedural memory into one connected graph rather than three separate stores.

nodes.label: Episodic Memory
nodes.rationale: Persistent conversation/session history stored as :Episode nodes linked via [:MODIFIED] edges to changed ConceptNodes.

nodes.label: Procedural Memory
nodes.rationale: Learned engineering guardrails stored as :Playbook nodes; written when a Senior Fix is applied so future agents inherit rules automatically.

nodes.label: Semantic Memory
nodes.rationale: Structured architectural knowledge stored as :ConceptNode nodes indexed across 17 Domain Lenses x 6 persona levels.

nodes.label: 3-Tier Agent Memory
nodes.rationale: Memory architecture combining Episodic (:Episode), Semantic (:ConceptNode), and Procedural (:Playbook) memory tiers in FalkorDB.

nodes.label: Real FalkorDB instance (Docker)
nodes.rationale: Hackathon rule 12 requires the graph database to do real work, so a real FalkorDB must answer a real query before any memory model is real.

nodes.label: FalkorDB speaks the Redis protocol on port 6379
nodes.norm_label: falkordb speaks the redis protocol on port 6379
nodes.rationale: Queries are issued as OpenCypher via GRAPH.QUERY/GRAPH.RO_QUERY over the Redis channel, which is why the official FalkorDB client connects on 6379.

nodes.label: Five Cypher memory clauses (CREATE, MERGE, MATCH, WHERE, RETURN)
nodes.norm_label: five cypher memory clauses (create, merge, match, where, return)
nodes.rationale: These clauses carry almost all memory work and let the learner read the simulated backend and tell what each query is meant to do.

nodes.label: MERGE as the memory-write primitive
nodes.rationale: Memory writes retry, so MERGE's idempotent match-or-create prevents duplicate facts where CREATE would duplicate on every re-run.

nodes.label: Cross-tier linking edges
nodes.rationale: Edges like Turn-MENTIONS->Entity (episodic-semantic) and Turn-USED->Tool (episodic-procedural) turn three data piles into one traversable connected graph.

nodes.label: Node families of the memory model
nodes.norm_label: node families of the memory model
nodes.rationale: User/Session/Turn (episodic), Entity/Fact (semantic), Tool/Workflow (procedural) are filled in by later lessons.

nodes.label: Idempotent episodic turn write (MERGE + ON CREATE SET)
nodes.norm_label: idempotent episodic turn write (merge + on create set)
nodes.rationale: MERGE on identity with ON CREATE SET for data lets a turn be written idempotently so re-runs never duplicate.

nodes.label: Bounded relational recall query
nodes.rationale: MATCH one user/topic with ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT N is bounded and traversable, unlike replaying an unbounded raw transcript.

nodes.label: LLM entity/relationship extraction into MERGE
nodes.rationale: An LLM extracts entities and relationships from a message; each entity becomes a node and each relationship a typed edge, MERGEd idempotently.

nodes.label: Provenance edges (MENTIONED_IN)
nodes.rationale: GraphRAG-SDK keeps MENTIONED_IN edges linking entity mentions to source chunks, preserving provenance and joining semantic to episodic nodes.

nodes.label: Playbook Guardrail
nodes.rationale: Named workflow node with ordered steps wiring handleApplySeniorFix to a graph lookup instead of a fresh guess.

nodes.label: Task-type lookup / guardrail
nodes.rationale: If the MATCH by task_type returns no rows, there is no stored playbook and the agent falls back to reasoning: no stored playbook, no automatic replay.

nodes.label: Workflow subgraph (Workflow -HAS_STEP-> Step -USES-> Tool)
nodes.rationale: A queryable, ordered structure that improves as successful runs are MERGEd in, unlike a flat prompt the agent must re-reason over.

nodes.label: What to Measure
nodes.rationale: No trusted third-party benchmark exists for this workload, so produce your own: write/read latency percentiles, error rate under N writers, throughput knee, and cross-tenant leakage.

nodes.label: Connection Usage
nodes.rationale: Create the client once and share it; concurrency is bounded by the server-side thread pool, not by how many sockets are opened.

nodes.label: MERGE for Idempotent Writes
nodes.rationale: MERGE matches a pattern or creates it, so a retried or duplicate write binds to the existing node instead of forking a second one; merge each entity in its own clause.

nodes.label: Write-Heavy Read-Modify-Write Loop
nodes.rationale: Each step per agent appends an episodic node, often a semantic update and a handoff, so the workload skews to many small writes with a traversal on every read.

nodes.label: Agent-Memory Cypher Snippets
nodes.rationale: Upsert, recall last N turns, find all facts about an entity, and fetch a workflow's ordered steps — the four read/write patterns behind the three memory tiers.

nodes.label: MERGE Clause
nodes.rationale: Matches the pattern or creates it — the basis of idempotent memory writes; use ON CREATE SET / ON MATCH SET and merge one entity per clause to avoid duplicating path endpoints.

nodes.label: Agent Node
nodes.rationale: One member of the four-agent squad with a role and persona level; part of the coordination layer.

nodes.label: Entity Node
nodes.rationale: An extracted domain object that is durable and independent of any one interaction — the semantic tier.

nodes.label: Fact Node
nodes.rationale: A durable assertion about the domain linked to the entity it concerns and the turn it was derived from.

nodes.label: Handoff Node
nodes.rationale: An event node recording transfer of state and responsibility, with status in {PENDING, COMPLETED, ALERT_RAISED, PLAYBOOK_ENFORCED}.

nodes.label: MERGE-Based Schema Writes
nodes.rationale: All writes use MERGE for idempotent memory writes, with indexes on MERGE-keyed properties to keep writes off full-graph scans.

nodes.label: Session Node
nodes.rationale: A contiguous conversation that groups turns and gives persistent conversation history a home.

nodes.label: Step Node
nodes.rationale: One action inside a workflow; steps are chained into a subgraph the agent can replay.

nodes.label: Tool Node
nodes.rationale: A callable capability such as a Cypher query template, an API, or a graph algorithm.

nodes.label: Topic Node
nodes.rationale: A subject label that ties episodic turns and semantic entities together for cross-session recall.

nodes.label: Turn Node
nodes.rationale: A single message/event with role in {user, agent, tool}; the atomic episodic record.

nodes.label: User Node
nodes.rationale: The actor, linked to past interactions so the agent can recall what happened last time.

nodes.label: Workflow Node
nodes.rationale: A reusable, re-executable sequence of steps — the stored pattern of a successful strategy that is the procedural tier.

nodes.label: Exit criterion
nodes.rationale: The single specific verifiable check that defines when a task is done, stated before work begins.

nodes.label: Reversible decision
nodes.rationale: A choice cheap to undo, so make it fast; its opposite deserves deliberate analysis.

nodes.label: Spec card
nodes.rationale: Five-line task brief handed to an agent instead of a vague wish.

nodes.label: Compounding Error
nodes.rationale: A silent error at step three is inherited by steps four through ten, so the whole run must be redone; verify-per-step keeps every failure local.

nodes.label: Evidence Before Assertions
nodes.rationale: When the agent says done that is a claim; the command and its raw output are the evidence. Done without output is a wish.

nodes.label: Health-Check Command
nodes.rationale: A script such as npm run health prints a node count, proving the FalkorDB connection works; run it after every change and never accept 'done' without its output.

nodes.label: Per-Action Verification
nodes.rationale: A quick, specific check right after each state-changing action keeps failures local so a fix costs one step instead of the session.

nodes.label: Verify Every Step
nodes.rationale: An agent doing ten steps checked only at the end cannot be trusted; errors compound (5% per-step becomes ~40% wrong by step ten), so verification must be immediate and local.

nodes.label: verify: line
nodes.rationale: Each step of a task spec carries a specific, checkable assertion (file X exists and contains Y), never 'looks good'.

nodes.label: Buy Information When Uncertainty Could Change the Decision
nodes.norm_label: buy information when uncertainty could change the decision
nodes.rationale: Do not spend effort obtaining information that cannot change the decision; but if cheap evidence exists, run it and let the result decide rather than the vibe.

nodes.label: Changeability
nodes.rationale: How expensive a decision is to reverse after commitment: if expensive, get it right before committing; if cheap, do not spend more avoiding error than the error costs to correct.

nodes.label: Decide Under Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Spend judgment in proportion to what reversal would cost; the AI should give options, not a verdict, because you own the decision and must explain it.

nodes.label: Decision Record
nodes.rationale: Three lines (DECISION, WHY, REVERSE) kept in docs/decisions.md become the answer to 'why did you pick X?' during judging and satisfy rule 12.

nodes.label: Expensive-to-Reverse Decision
nodes.rationale: Interfaces, persistent data representations, architectural boundaries, security protocols, and external integrations can become expensive or effectively irreversible and so deserve deliberate reasoning.

nodes.label: Graph Schema Decision
nodes.rationale: Node labels, relationship types, and property keys are a persistent data representation every stored memory and Cypher query depends on, so changes are expensive to reverse.

nodes.label: Mandatory Decision
nodes.rationale: Track, key-focus features, and submission format are not a choice; build to spec and do not reopen.

nodes.label: Builder Role
nodes.rationale: Builds against the system, stops at the first blocker and reports it, and never touches core code; because it cannot rationalize bugs away it experiences them the way a real user would.

nodes.label: Fixer Role
nodes.rationale: Reads blocker reports and fixes core code, and never touches the app being built — a structural boundary that prevents fixes far from the fault.

nodes.label: Issue Report
nodes.rationale: A structured report (call, expected, actual, blocked) the builder writes and stops on instead of improvising; it doubles as a handoff record.

nodes.label: Reviewer Role
nodes.rationale: Read-only independent verification that finds problems and changes nothing, so it is not the author's context.

nodes.label: Role Card
nodes.rationale: The boundary is the prompt: it names the file the role may touch, the autonomy tier, the checkpoint, and the exact stop-and-report rule.

nodes.label: Compartmentalize Roles & Autonomy
nodes.rationale: One session for planning, coding, testing, and debugging makes the agent improvise in layers it should never touch; split into roles with hard boundaries and match autonomy to risk.

nodes.label: Tier 1 — Interactive
nodes.rationale: The agent proposes and you approve every step; best for novel decisions, architecture, and anything where the wrong choice is expensive.

nodes.label: Tier 2 — Bounded Sprint
nodes.rationale: The agent works independently and reports at a defined checkpoint; best for implementing a spec you already wrote, such as wiring write_turn.

nodes.label: Tier 3 — Unattended
nodes.rationale: The agent runs alone and you review the result; best for purely mechanical tasks such as renames, formatting, and doc updates.

nodes.label: Four-Part Bug Report
nodes.rationale: A good report is itself a debugging tool: expected, observed, steps to reproduce, and what you already tried — writing it forces the precision a vague plea skips.

nodes.label: Decision-Bearing Commit
nodes.rationale: A commit message carrying what was built, the design decision, why, and the exit evidence — with the word 'decision' so git log --grep finds it.

nodes.label: Git as the Agent's Long-Term Memory
nodes.norm_label: git as the agent's long-term memory
nodes.rationale: The AI does not remember what it decided and will re-derive it differently, so the decision must live in the repo's history rather than in session logs or sticky notes.

nodes.label: Rubber-Duck at 30 Minutes
nodes.rationale: After 30 minutes without progress, explain the problem out loud to force examination of assumptions; after half a day bring a fresh reader with what you tried and your best hypothesis.

nodes.label: Four-Command Session-Open Protocol
nodes.rationale: Open every session by reading the repo as memory: recent log, decision log grep, recent file diff, and the health-check command proving the instance is up.

nodes.label: Write for Future-You & Ask Like a Senior
nodes.norm_label: write for future-you & ask like a senior
nodes.rationale: Every new agent session starts cold, so two habits fix drift: a commit history written as a briefing and questions sharp enough to act on at the first try.

nodes.label: Milestone E — Work Like a Senior Engineer
nodes.norm_label: milestone e — work like a senior engineer
nodes.rationale: The thesis is that you cannot prompt better than you can think; these habits come first and govern every lesson below.

nodes.label: Exit-Criterion Anti-Patterns
nodes.rationale: Activity descriptions ('wire up FalkorDB'), implementation details ('uses MERGE'), and unverifiable claims ('memory works') are not exit criteria.

nodes.label: Exit-Criterion Derivation Recipe
nodes.rationale: Restate what as behaviour, name the observer, write Given/When/Then, attach the exact command, and add the load-bearing check plus one failure case.

nodes.label: Given / When / Then
nodes.rationale: Given state, when one action, then one observable result — if a spec cannot be written as a single Given/When/Then it is too vague or too big.

nodes.label: Autonomy Tiers
nodes.rationale: Interactive, bounded sprint, and unattended batch — decide the tier before the task and write it at the top of the spec.

nodes.label: The Build Loop
nodes.rationale: Plan, Spec, Context, Build, Verify, Commit — six gates every task passes; skipping a gate wastes a hackathon hour rebuilding something.

nodes.label: Context Budget (ALWAYS / ON DEMAND / NEVER)
nodes.rationale: Too little context causes hallucination and too much causes lost focus, so context is controlled in three buckets; context engineering beats prompt phrasing by a wide margin.

nodes.label: The Debugging Loop
nodes.rationale: Reproduce before theorizing, force three ranked hypotheses with claim/test/prediction, run the cheapest discriminating test, then fix the root cause with a regression test.

nodes.label: Decision Rubric
nodes.rationale: Ask whether a decision is mandatory, reversible or irreversible, what evidence decides it, and its cost-of-change and decomposability.

nodes.label: Weak to Senior Prompt Library
nodes.rationale: Eight weak-to-senior swaps that carry the spec card, context bucket, boundaries, and verify line as templates rather than scripts.

nodes.label: Question Templates
nodes.rationale: Reusable bug-report, explain, and review templates that force expected/observed/repro precision and constrain output.

nodes.label: Senior Questions Checklist
nodes.rationale: The questions a senior asks before starting — exit criterion, failure modes, reversibility, boundaries, context budget, tier, bottleneck, verification, feedback loops.

nodes.label: Autonomy tier
nodes.rationale: Level of oversight a task receives: Tier 1 interactive, Tier 2 bounded sprint, Tier 3 unattended batch.

nodes.label: Horizontal slab
nodes.rationale: One layer built across every feature before the next starts, so nothing works until all layers are done.

nodes.label: Systems thinking
nodes.rationale: Reasoning about boundaries, data flow, feedback loops, and failure modes rather than isolated components.

nodes.label: Vertical slice
nodes.rationale: One thin feature built through every layer end-to-end so it is independently demoable and verifiable.

nodes.label: Retry Storm
nodes.rationale: The retry mechanism designed to improve reliability prevents recovery: each straggler retry adds load, slows the graph, and triggers more retries.

nodes.label: Decomposability
nodes.rationale: Ask whether a partial system produces useful evidence before the whole exists; the smaller the portion required, the more opportunities for early learning.

nodes.label: Append-over-Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Never rewrite a whole session node each turn; append a small Turn node and link it so writes stay O(1) in size and independent per turn.

nodes.label: Hot-Node Avoidance
nodes.rationale: A single Session or User node every writer updates is a serialization point; keep the fan-in node read-mostly and push volatile parts out to appended nodes.

nodes.label: Provenance via Event Node Timestamp
nodes.rationale: Carry the episodic event node's ts and origin back up the path instead of discarding it; that timestamp is the citation that makes an answer sourced.

nodes.label: Exit Criterion (Verifiable Check)
nodes.rationale: The highest-leverage line: a specific verifiable check like a submit-cookie-redirect beats 'feature works' because it cannot be argued with.

nodes.label: Context budget
nodes.rationale: Deliberate split of what a model always sees, sees on demand, and never sees.

nodes.label: Reproduce (repro)
nodes.rationale: Triggering a bug on demand, the precondition for any fix.

nodes.label: Root cause
nodes.rationale: The condition that, if fixed, prevents the defect recurring, as opposed to the symptom.

nodes.label: Rule 12 — Understand and Explain Submitted Code
nodes.community_name: Rule 12 — Understand and Explain Submitted Code
nodes.norm_label: rule 12 — understand and explain submitted code

nodes.label: Regression test
nodes.rationale: Test written from the reproduction so a fixed defect cannot silently return.

nodes.label: Confident Fix for an Unreproduced Bug
nodes.norm_label: confident fix for an unreproduced bug
nodes.rationale: The single most common way AI-assisted debugging goes wrong is the model proposing a confident fix for a bug nobody reproduced.

nodes.label: Rank by Likelihood x Ease of Test
nodes.norm_label: rank by likelihood x ease of test
nodes.rationale: A probably-right hypothesis that takes four hours to test is a worse next move than a possibly-right one that takes thirty seconds.

nodes.label: Reproduce Reliably
nodes.rationale: Nail expected, observed (the exact error text), and the minimal sequence; if you cannot trigger it on demand, finding a reliable repro is the whole task.

nodes.label: Fix the Root Cause, Not the Symptom
nodes.norm_label: fix the root cause, not the symptom

nodes.label: Force Three Hypotheses
nodes.rationale: Even when one hypothesis feels obvious, forcing three with a written prediction keeps you honest.

nodes.label: Append a Turn, Don't Rewrite a Session
nodes.norm_label: append a turn, don't rewrite a session
nodes.rationale: A new Turn is an independent write; rewriting a whole session re-touches one node every other writer also touches and its cost grows with history.

nodes.label: Interface-First Contract
nodes.rationale: Interfaces accumulate users and become effectively irreversible, so lock the contract and keep bodies revisable.

nodes.label: Handoff
nodes.rationale: Transfer of state and responsibility between agents, recorded in the graph so the receiver knows what was done and why.

nodes.label: Idempotent MERGE Write
nodes.rationale: MERGE matches a pattern or creates it if absent, making memory writes idempotent and re-runnable.

nodes.label: Idempotent MERGE Writes
nodes.rationale: A retried or duplicated write does not create a second node when keyed with MERGE; merge each node separately so a path merge cannot duplicate an endpoint.

nodes.label: Documented GAP: shared multi-agent handoff patterns
nodes.norm_label: documented gap: shared multi-agent handoff patterns
nodes.rationale: No trusted source specifies a shared handoff/shared-state pattern over FalkorDB, so the handoff-ledger design is the learner's own original contribution.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Speaks RESP over TCP
nodes.rationale: Browsers can only make HTTP requests but cannot open arbitrary TCP sockets, so a Node process must hold the FalkorDB connection and expose it over HTTP.

nodes.label: Prompt Quality Is Capped by Judgment
nodes.norm_label: prompt quality is capped by judgment
nodes.rationale: Phrasing tweaks yield 5-10% gains while engineering context and success criteria yield 20-45% faster cycles, so the goal is to become the engineer who knows what done means.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Development
nodes.rationale: A mini-spec per task prevents the agent doing too little, too much, or something technically correct but wrong for your context.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.rationale: The lever that moves AI output is what the model can see when it runs, not how the request is phrased; structured context pipelines yield 20-45% faster cycles.

nodes.label: NEVER Context Bucket
nodes.rationale: Dumping the whole codebase overwhelms the agent, which loses focus and hallucinates details from the wrong files.

nodes.label: Isolation vs. Cross-Tenant Analytics Trade-off
nodes.rationale: One-graph-per-tenant buys isolation and operational simplicity but costs cross-tenant analytics, since you cannot MATCH across graphs in a single query.

nodes.label: One Graph Per Tenant
nodes.rationale: Isolation is structural: a tenant's whole agent memory lives in a separate graph, so no query leaks across tenants and no tenant filter is required.

nodes.label: Bubble-Up Senior Guardian Alerting
nodes.rationale: L4 CRITICAL risks are linked to the L0 feature nodes they endanger via [:ENDANGERS] edges, so a non-technical Vibe Coder sees a plain-English safety alert on their own button and can apply a one-click fix.

nodes.label: Builder Maturity Levels (L0-L5)
nodes.rationale: Progressive depth control: a single graph slice is presented at the right abstraction for a Vibe Coder (L0) up to a Principal/Researcher (L5), avoiding both overwhelming beginners and boring experts.

nodes.label: Cognitive Debt
nodes.rationale: Central problem the app solves: builders ship AI-generated code they do not understand, accumulating hidden architectural/security/spend risk. GraphSync surfaces this hidden debt by translating the same system at six maturity levels instead of hiding complexity entirely.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Agent Memory
nodes.rationale: Three-tier memory model stored in FalkorDB - Episodic (:Episode), Semantic (:ConceptNode), Procedural (:Playbook) - so agents persist what happened, what the system is, and what rules they learned.

nodes.label: 4-Agent FalkorDB Squad
nodes.rationale: Four coordinating agents partition the L0-L5 work - VibeArchitect (L0-L1), FullStackBuilder (L2-L3), SeniorAuditor (L4), PrincipalResearcher (L5) - sharing one FalkorDB graph, mirroring how a real engineering org delegates by seniority.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Graph Isolation
nodes.rationale: Each user/project keeps its own memory partition (select_graph topology) so agent learning and playbooks never leak across tenants; the UI switches tenants via a FalkorDB multigraph selector.

nodes.label: Procedural Memory Playbook Guardrails
nodes.rationale: When a user applies a senior fix, a :Playbook rule is written so future agent runs query Procedural Memory first and auto-inject rate limiting - turning a one-time mistake into durable organizational learning.

nodes.label: L0-L5 Semantic Concept Nodes
nodes.rationale: Every architecture concept is one :ConceptNode tagged with a persona_level and a domain lens, linked by [:DEEPER_AT] into a depth chain, so the same knowledge can be traversed or filtered at any maturity/domain slice.

nodes.label: Multi-graph / multi-tenant topology
nodes.rationale: FalkorDB's ability to hold thousands of isolated graphs in one instance so each tenant gets a separate memory graph without a separate deployment.

nodes.label: CREATE Clause
nodes.rationale: Always creates new nodes/edges and never checks for duplicates, so it silently multiplies nodes if used for turns; reserve it for genuinely new entities.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Cypher
nodes.rationale: The query language used to read and write the Track 02 agent-memory graph; every clause and example is from the official FalkorDB Cypher reference.

nodes.label: Cypher Gotchas
nodes.rationale: Case-sensitive labels and keys, LIMIT does not restrict eager writes, DELETE behaves like DETACH DELETE, and returning a bound entity returns the whole node.

nodes.label: Cypher Parameters
nodes.rationale: Always pass $param through the client's native parameterization instead of pasting user input into the query string.

nodes.label: FalkorDB-Is-Load-Bearing Check
nodes.rationale: Every Track 02 feature needs proof FalkorDB does real work (rule 3): with FalkorDB stopped the app must error rather than silently keep working.

nodes.label: De-Scope List
nodes.rationale: Auth, billing, advanced graph algorithms, other tracks, mobile, production hardening, and horizontal scaling are out of scope because every hour not proving a key-focus point is wasted.

nodes.label: Differentiators
nodes.rationale: Live memory visualization, handoff ledger timeline, tenant switcher, concurrency panel, and persona lenses make the key-focus claims visible to judges.

nodes.label: Required MVP Features
nodes.rationale: Ten features from a real FalkorDB connection through the three memory tiers, persistence, handoffs, isolation, concurrency, explainability, and the cockpit.

nodes.label: Submission Artifacts (rule 10)
nodes.rationale: Public repo, README with setup and the graph data model, the real Cypher queries, a demo video, deployment or local setup, the track, and AI-assistant disclosure.

nodes.label: The Three-Tier Trick
nodes.rationale: Show episodic, semantic, and procedural memory as one connected graph; three separate stores look like three demos, one connected graph looks like a memory system.

nodes.label: :HANDED_TO Relationship
nodes.rationale: A direct typed edge between agents carrying a timestamp; the coordination skeleton of the model.

nodes.label: Per-Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Each tenant gets its own graph key; because every write is scoped to a graph, isolation is a structural property rather than a query filter.

nodes.label: Tenant Node
nodes.rationale: An isolation boundary; one Tenant maps to one FalkorDB graph key and is the root of the multi-graph topology.

nodes.label: Two-Minute Demo Shot List
nodes.rationale: Frame it, show three-tier memory, persistence, handoff, concurrency, isolation, then the rule-3 line — every key-focus point visible on camera.

nodes.label: Track 02 Key-Focus Points
nodes.rationale: Episodic, semantic, and procedural memory, persistent conversation history, shared state and handoffs, high-concurrency reads and writes, and separate memory per user or tenant.

nodes.label: Rule 10 Submission Items
nodes.rationale: Public repo, README with setup and graph data model, the load-bearing Cypher queries, a demo video, deployment or local setup, and the track being entered.

nodes.label: The Real-Work Test (rule 3)
nodes.rationale: If FalkorDB were removed and the product still worked, the graph is decoration; with it stopped, recall, handoffs, and isolation must all fail.

nodes.label: Track 02 Curriculum
nodes.rationale: Short lessons each with a tangible win; Milestone E installs the engineering judgment that governs every other lesson.

nodes.label: Track 02 Feature Set
nodes.rationale: Everything traces to the official Track 02 brief or the hackathon rules; build the 10 MVP features, prove each, add 2-3 differentiators, submit the 7 artifacts.

nodes.label: Track 02 Check-off List
nodes.rationale: A scannable page: for each key-focus point the evidence to show, then the rule 10 submission items, the rule 3 real-work test, and a two-minute demo shot list.
